question.problem:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}-4y=4,\,y(0)=1,\,{y}^{′}(0)=4
$$

is given by

$$
{s}^{2}Y(s)-s-4-4Y(s)=\frac{4}{s}.
$$

The solution is $y(t)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{2}Y(s)-s-4-4Y(s) & =\frac{4}{s} \\ ({s}^{2}-4)Y(s) & =\frac{4}{s}+s+4 \\ ({s}^{2}-4)Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}+4s+4}{s} \\ (s-2)(s+2)Y(s) & =\frac{(s+2)^{2}}{s} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{s+2}{s(s-2)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{2}{s-2}-\frac{1}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

which is valid for $s>2.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{2}{s-2}-\frac{1}{s}\} \\ y(t) & =2{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-2}\}-{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\} \\ y(t) & =2{e}^{2t}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
